title: Profiling Hallucinations in Frontier LLMs for Entity Linking to Medical Ontologies
abstract: arXiv:2611.18595v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into healthcare promises to revolutionize clinical documentation and interoperability, yet reliability remains a concern. This study presents a comprehensive analysis of hallucinations by frontier LLMs tasked with mapping clinical text to SNOMED CT. Through rigorous experimentation, we identify a critical reliability gap: LLMs hallucinate medical codes at a rate that currently renders them unsuitable for autonomous clinical coding applications. Paradoxically, constraining models to use ground-truth mention spans exacerbates, rather than mitigates, these hallucinations. We further contribute a taxonomy of hallucination types--including deprecated codes and cross-ontology errors--and demonstrate that general-purpose LLMs significantly underperform compared to specialized zero-shot entity linking approaches. These findings underscore the need for robust verification mechanisms before clinical

translated_title: 前沿大语言模型在医学本体实体链接任务中的幻觉剖析
translated_abstract: 将大语言模型（LLM）整合到医疗保健领域有望彻底改变临床文档记录和互操作性，但其可靠性仍令人担忧。本研究对前沿LLM在将临床文本映射到SNOMED CT任务中产生的幻觉进行了全面分析。通过严格的实验，我们发现了一个关键的可靠性差距：LLM产生医学编码幻觉的比率目前使其不适用于自主临床编码应用。矛盾的是，将模型约束为使用真实标注的提及片段反而会加剧而非缓解这些幻觉。我们进一步提出了一个幻觉类型的分类体系——包括已弃用编码和跨本体错误——并证明通用LLM的表现显著逊色于专门的零样本实体链接方法。这些发现强调了在临床应用之前需要健全的验证机制。
tldr: 本研究系统剖析了前沿大语言模型在将临床文本映射到SNOMED CT时的幻觉问题，发现其幻觉率过高而不适合自主临床编码应用，且约束使用真实提及片段反而会加剧幻觉，通用LLM的表现显著逊色于专门的零样本实体链接方法。
en_tdlr: This study systematically profiles hallucinations in frontier LLMs for mapping clinical text to SNOMED CT, finding that their hallucination rates render them unsuitable for autonomous clinical coding, that constraining models to ground-truth mention spans paradoxically exacerbates hallucinations, and that general-purpose LLMs significantly underperform specialized zero-shot entity linking approaches.
